sections.heading: Apostille or embassy legalisation?
sections.text:
If a UK document will be used abroad, the receiving country usually needs proof it is genuine. For countries in the Hague Apostille Convention, including India, China, Saudi Arabia and most of Europe, an apostille from the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) is enough.

For countries outside the Convention, such as the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Kuwait, the document is apostilled first and then legalised by that country's embassy in London.

sections.heading: Documents we legalise
sections.text:
We regularly handle:
- Degree certificates and transcripts
- Police certificates (DBS and ACRO)
- Birth, marriage and death certificates
- Company documents, such as certificates of incorporation, powers of attorney and commercial invoices
- Medical and employment letters

Some documents must be certified by a UK solicitor or notary before the FCDO will apostille them. We arrange this for you.

sections.heading: For work visas abroad
sections.text: Many work visas, such as for Saudi Arabia, the UAE and China, need degree certificates and police checks legalised before the visa is issued. We handle the legalisation and the visa together so nothing is missed.

sections.heading: Document legalisation in Manchester
sections.text: We're based in Manchester city centre and help travellers and businesses across the North West and the rest of the UK. Most travel visa applications can be handled by post and email, so you don't need to visit us in person.
